question: What is the 'two-minute rule' for starting a habit?
answer: Shrink the new habit until it takes two minutes: 'read before bed' becomes 'read one page', 'go running' becomes 'put on your running shoes'. Clear's argument is that a habit has to be established before it can be improved, and the hardest part is the start, so make the start almost too easy to skip.
move: Make the first step so small you can't say no to it.
simply: Don't promise to tidy your whole room. Promise to pick up one sock. Usually you'll keep going.
why: Big plans fail on tired days. A two-minute version keeps the chain unbroken until it grows on its own.
